question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=26 x^{2} + 13.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
f'(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(26 x^{2} + 13\right)=52 x
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(3,247):$

$$
m=f'(3)=156
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line is

$$
m'=-\frac{1}{m}=- \frac{1}{156}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-\left(247\right)&=- \frac{1}{156}\left(x-\left(3\right)\right) \\ x+156\cdot y&=38535.\end{aligned}
$$
